title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II
description:
# Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

Given a singly linked list sorted in nondecreasing order, remove every node whose value occurs more than once in the original list. Retain only values that originally occurred exactly once, preserving order, and return the head.

For example, `1 -> 2 -> 2 -> 3` becomes `1 -> 3`: both nodes with value `2` are removed. Return `null` if no value remains.

Example arrays display values in `next` order; `[]` denotes an empty list (`null`). A node stores its value in `val` and its next node in `next`. Use node objects for list parameters and results as shown in the initial code.

## Example 1:

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,3,4,4,5]
**Output:** [1,2,5]
**Explanation:** Values `3` and `4` each appear more than once, so all `3` and `4` nodes are removed.

## Example 2:

**Input:** head = [1,1,1,2,3]
**Output:** [2,3]
**Explanation:** Every `1` node belongs to a duplicate group, so the returned list starts at `2`.

## Constraints:

* The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[0, 300]`.
* `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`
* The list is sorted in ascending order.
* Values that appear more than once must be removed completely, not compressed to one copy.

solutions.name: Sentinel Predecessor Group Skip
solutions.description:
## Approach

Place a sentinel before the original head and keep `prev` at the tail of the confirmed distinct prefix. For each value group, scan `curr` to the last node in that group. If the group had duplicates, connect `prev.next` to the first node after the group; otherwise advance `prev` to keep the singleton.

## Key Insight

The predecessor of a duplicate group must stay outside the group, because the entire group is removed. The sentinel makes this uniform when the group to delete starts at the original head.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Run-Length Tail Relink
solutions.description:
## Approach

Read the list one value run at a time. Store the first node of the run, count how many nodes have that value, and advance the read pointer past the run. If the count is one, attach that first node to the answer tail; otherwise discard the whole run. Finally truncate the tail.

## Key Insight

The sorted input turns the problem into run classification. A run of length one is kept, while a run of length greater than one contributes no node at all.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Duplicate Group Removal
solutions.description:
## Approach

If the current head starts a duplicate group, remember its value, skip every node with that value, and recursively solve the suffix. If the head is a singleton, keep it and recursively clean `head.next`.

## Key Insight

The recursive branch must skip all nodes of a repeated value before recursing. Keeping one representative would solve the previous problem, not this one.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n) recursion stack

solutions.name: Frequency Map Rebuild
solutions.description:
## Approach

First count how many times each value appears. Then traverse the original list again and append a newly allocated node only for values whose count is exactly one.

## Key Insight

This route deliberately avoids pointer edge cases. It is less space-efficient, but it directly encodes the rule that only globally unique values survive.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Two-Pointer Singleton Value Compaction
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan runs with `read`, and reuse the first nodes of the original list as write slots for singleton values only. When a run has length one, write that value into the next output slot. If no singleton exists, return `null`; otherwise truncate after the last written node.

## Key Insight

This is an array-style compaction variant for linked lists. It is useful as a contrast because it removes duplicate groups by copying surviving values rather than by preserving original node identity.

## Complexity Analysis

- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)
